newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN PUT CRISIS BEHIND THEM TO GO TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN PUT CRISIS BEHIND THEM TO GO TOP.

text.p: George Weah and Roberto Baggio helped Italian champions Milan put successive league and European Cup defeats behind them on Sunday to defeat Napoli 3-1 and open a one-point lead at the top of serie A.
With 12 points from six matches, the champions lie a point ahead of arch-rivals Inter, who will regain the lead if they beat Juventus at Turin in the eveningt match.
European champions Juventus, on 10 points, can go top if they defeat Inter in a clash between the only clubs in serie A who have never been relegated.
Giampiero Maini scored a late equaliser at Udinese for Vicenza who lead Roma, Parma, Bologna and Juventus in a group of five clubs tied for third place on 10 points.
With five defeats in 11 competitive matches, including a 3-0 thrashing at Roma in their last league outing, Milan started their match determined to shake off hints of crisis.
But it took 40 minutes for the breakthrough when Baggio's inswinging free-kick creating havoc in the Napoli defence allowing Weah to turn home his sixth goal of the season.
Straight after the break, Weah combined neatly with Marco Simone to put Milan two up only for Brazilian Andre Cruz to find another hole in the champions' defence with a 20-metre shot.
But with Napoli threatening a second goal, Baggio showed glimpses of his old magic to escape his marker in the penalty area and slot Milan's third past Giuseppe Taglialatela.

"It wasn't easy," said club president Silvio Berlusconi. "But finally I saw a convincing Milan performance. Let's not forget that we have players like (Franco) Baresi and (Dejan) Savicevic out of the side."
Perugia coach Giovanni Galeone, at odds with club owner Luciano Gaucci, came out of hospital after suffering heart pains and was told to win at Parma or leave.
In a remarkable performance, Galeone's players rallied to their besieged manager's aid, scoring two goals in a four minute spell to inflict Parma's first home defeat of the season.

Federico Giunti, who caught Luca Bucci by surprise with his 21st minute long-range effort, and Carmine Gautieri's header in the 25th, gave Parma a double shock from which they never really recovered. Enrico Chiesa's injury-time effort came too late.
Salvatore Giunta sowed the seeds of Roma's second defeat in a week by curling a left-foot shot past goalkeeper Giorgio Sterchele from the edge of the area on the half-hour.

The visitors fought their way back into the game with Marco Delvecchio's 51st minute equaliser only for Pierluigi Orlandini's 80th minute effort to give Verona their first win of the season and lift them off the bottom of the table.

With Bologna due to meet traditional rivals Fiorentina in next week's Italian Cup match, club president Giuseppe Gazzoni had billed Sunday's match at the Dall'Ara as a dress rehearsel for the two club's traditionally hostile fans.
He was not impressed. Florentine supporters celebrated Gabriel Batistuta's spectacular 30-metre opener in a 2-0 victory for the visitors by launching flares at Bologna fans.

When goalkeeper Luca Marchegiani was given his matching orders after five minutes for handling outside the penalty area, Lazio's poor start to the season - five points in as many matches - looked set to continue against Cagliari.
But Czech Paolo Nedved's second goal in two matches and Giuseppe Signori's 50th minute solo effort gave Lazio a remarkable win, despite Giacomo Banchelli's late effort.
